deviations.observed: pid 15367 alive about an hour after done, 0% CPU, with its caffeinate child 15384; run.lock released; run.json written 03:14:36Z

diagnosis.sample: macOS sample of 15367 (read-only, 1 s): the main thread is in dyld exit -> libsystem_c exit -> __cxa_finalize_ranges -> uv__threadpool_cleanup -> uv_thread_join -> _pthread_join (__ulock_wait); 3 libuv-worker threads parked in uv_cond_wait; the inspector I/O thread in uv_sem_wait. Node 22.22.0, libuv 1.51.0, macOS 26.5.
diagnosis.meaning: main() had returned, the event loop had ended and C exit() was running static destructors: libuv's threadpool cleanup posted its exit message and is joining a worker that never woke. Not a keep-alive agent (no TCP socket open: lsof shows only the log, two pipes, a kqueue, a unix socket and a com.apple.netsrc control socket), not the progress interval (unref'd and cleared), not caffeinate (it waits for 15367 with -w; it is the effect, not the cause). No JS can run, so nothing more can be written.
diagnosis.reproduced: no: a 60-parcel whole-seed run (scratch runs and Loader directories) exited with code 0 within a second of done (both at 04:25:26Z), as did the three phase A dry runs; the stall is intermittent and inside Node's own teardown
diagnosis.fix: kit 6107969: main() flushes stdout and stderr, arms a detached exit watchdog (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL, if the runner is still alive 30 s after its exit and its command still names t5-run) and calls process.exit(code) on every path; tested with a SIGTERM-ignoring stand-in and a real runner child with a leaked ref'd handle (fails without the fix by timeout)
diagnosis.safe_to_stop: yes: run-state finished, run.lock released, run.json fsynced, the Loader CURRENT points at the run, no elephant-cli child, the process holds only the log open for writing and is past the end of main; kill 15367 (SIGTERM), and kill -9 15367 if it is still there after 5 s (a process stuck in exit may not act on SIGTERM); caffeinate 15384 ends with it

why_the_box_and_not_the_boundary.boundary: Census TIGERweb State_County layer 1, GEOID 48453 (GET https://tigerweb.geo.census.gov/arcgis/rest/services/TIGERweb/State_County/MapServer/1/query?where=GEOID='48453'&outSR=4326&f=geojson, 2026-10-19, 79,915 bytes, SHA-256 1656dd6d50e4e1bcdeec319d604abe47d2bfb629e746777378a9a0c407456a17, one ring of 1,955 vertices, extent -98.1730 to -97.3695 W, 30.0235 to 30.6282 N); a scratch check, not kept, never a record's source
why_the_box_and_not_the_boundary.the_12: 7 of the 12 have their centroid outside the line (9-967 m); every one has vertices inside it
why_the_box_and_not_the_boundary.conclusion: the line TCAD's parcel fabric follows is not the Census line: an exact boundary test would refuse 56 accounts the run published (TCAD appraises them, the TNR layer draws them), and a tolerance would have to be calibrated on the data. Not cheap and not proven, so the seed box: 0 of 373,513 geometries has any point outside it, and it contains the contract box, so it refuses nothing that passed. The other identity checks (seed county and FIPS, source hosts, request identifiers, address state) still keep a wrong-county record out.
